question.text: Which of the following fee-structure concepts is NOT a primary testable concept at the Cat I/II AIF manager level (XIX-D scope)?

answer.text: High-Water Mark crystallisation on daily-NAV basis

explanation.text: **The Logic:** HWM crystallisation on a daily-NAV basis is Cat III (hedge-fund-style) machinery. Cat I/II AIFs are illiquid, private-market, closed-ended funds using hurdle rate + deal-by-deal or end-of-fund waterfalls with catch-up and clawback. HWM appears in Chapter 6 mainly for CONTRAST; daily-NAV HWM is XIX-E territory. **The Trap:** A, B, D are all core Cat I/II fee-structure constructs. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D scope explicitly excludes Cat III fee mechanics. XIX-E (Cat III Managers) is where HWM crystallisation, daily NAV, and 2x leverage math are core tested content. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In LP conversations, explain the distinction clearly: Cat I/II uses illiquid-market waterfalls (hurdle + catch-up + clawback), Cat III uses liquid-market mechanics (HWM + daily NAV). Mixing the two in a pitch deck confuses sophisticated LPs.
